title: Missouri American Water Supports Local Heroes Through 2026 Firefighter Grant Program
summary: Nearly $50,000 awarded to Missouri fire departments and emergency response organizations. ST. LOUIS, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Missouri fire departments and emergency response organizations...
body_markdown:
*Nearly $50,000 awarded to Missouri fire departments and emergency response organizations.*


ST. LOUIS


, Sept. 17, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- Missouri fire departments and emergency response organizations will receive nearly $50,000 through Missouri American Water's[Firefighter Grant Program](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4776262-1&h=2964017229&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amwater.com%2Fmoaw%2FNews-Community%2FCommunity-Involvement%2Ffirefighter-grant-program&a=Firefighter+Grant+Program) . Supporting local firefighters means supporting safer, stronger communities. These grants help provide critical tools and training that allow departments to respond effectively when residents need them most.


"As a water provider, we recognize the important connection between reliable water infrastructure and effective fire protection. Our Firefighter Grant Program is one more way we support the local departments that help keep our communities safe, helping to ensure they have access to resources that strengthen emergency preparedness and response," said Rich Svindland, president of Missouri American Water.


Reliable water service is critical for fire protection, and Missouri American Water is investing nearly $510 million in 2026 to improve service and reliability. Many older water mains are upsized when replaced, increasing water flow to enhance fire protection. The company also maintains and annually tests more than 44,000 fire hydrants throughout the company's footprint.


"Our portable radios were purchased in 2018, and the batteries are beginning to reach the end of their lifespan," said Fire Chief Aaron Houk. "This grant will help us replace six batteries and maintain reliable communications for our firefighters on scenes until we can budget for additional replacements."


Approximately 380 grants have been awarded since the program began in 2016. Grants will be distributed to 48 fire departments across Missouri this year. To see a full list of 2026 grantees and learn more about the annual program,[click here](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4776262-1&h=1422995997&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amwater.com%2Fmoaw%2FNews-Community%2FCommunity-Involvement%2Ffirefighter-grant-program&a=click+here) .
